items.content_html:
Thousands of children in Gaza are grappling with the agony and disbelief of losing a parent.

The warmth and care of those who matter the most, stolen. No child should be left alone to fend for themself.
It is our responsibility and choice to stand by them now.

We are calling for donations to help us provide immediate relief and a lasting support system for 20,000 children.

Make a direct impact by sponsoring an orphan today.

Become an annual sponsor - $2,000

Become a monthly sponsor - $167

or choose your own amount, every contribution matters.

A full-scale humanitarian crisis needs an unmatched scale of support.

Here's how we are ramping up our efforts to ensure that donations will reach every orphan.

In partnership with Bank of Palestine Group, we have launched Noor’s Program to support 20,000 children orphaned by the war. Our target of 377 million dollars. to provide a comprehensive range of services that ensure these orphans can live with dignity, become active members of their communities, and build a better future for themselves.

We will be addressing several fronts from responding to immediate needs rising under the ongoing bombardment and aggression, to establishing a solid support system that the orphans can rely on until they reach the age of 18.

We have partnered with civil society organizations in Gaza that will help implement our various interventions, ensure direct access to the orphans and their families, as well as host activities in every locale. Meanwhile, our network of external experts will work alongside us to assess the program's needs, impact and progress.


This is our largest campaign for orphans to date. We count on every single contribution

Noor Orphans Program Data

Distribution percentages of orphans by governorate:

Every day

63 children in Gaza lose their parent

1 out 3

orphans are under 5 years

491

Orphans have been physically injured

Food & Clothing

Periodic meal vouchers and two clothing packages annually

Healthcare

Medical examination and treatment, disabled orphan rehabilitation, and assistive devices provision.

Education & Vocational Training

Tuition fees, school uniform and bag, supporting education, extracurricular activities, talent nurturing, and vocational education

Protection and Psychological Support

Individual and group sessions, as well as therapeutic recreational activities

Social Welfare

Fostering in orphanages or foster families

Mohamed: A boy who lost everything,
but still found a reason to smile.

After losing his father and suffering severe injuries, Mohamed’s smile returned when he received new clothes. 'When I wore the new clothes, I felt like there’s someone out there who still cares,' he says.

Oday’s Vision Fades,
But Hope Remains

With the loss of his father and the sight in one eye, Oday faced darkness. Your support gave his family the essentials to restore hope for the future.

About Taawon

Taawon is an independent collective of Palestinian entrepreneurs, business practitioners, scholars and thinkers, bound together across generations by our dedication for Palestine to persevere and thrive.

Since 1983, we have worked to help defend and preserve the Palestinian cause, our culture and our people, by empowering Palestinians and investing in building Palestine's human capital together with local civil society organizations and a growing network of global support.

Over the last 15 years, Taawon has supported 4,261 orphans across Gaza, doing so in collaboration with a network of civil society organizations who specialize in these areas. The approach has always been focused on providing a holistic intervention encompassing education, finance and physical and mental health for each child based on their individual needs.

We are available for your inquiries.
Email us at [email protected] 

Gaza's orphaned children are our collective responsibility.

Thousands of orphaned children in Gaza are left heartbroken and lost, too young to understand the pain of losing their parents.

Their families, their warmth, their security—taken away in an instant. This Ramadan, let’s not let them face the darkness alone. It is our duty, our choice, to be the light they need.

Help us deliver urgent relief and develop a sustainable support system for 20,000 orphans in Gaza.

Taawon Foundation is an independent, non-profit Palestinian organization founded in Geneva in 1983 as a development institution aimed at enhancing the capabilities of the Palestinian people, preserving their heritage and identity, and supporting their vibrant culture. This is achieved through the systematic identification of the needs and priorities of the Palestinian people and employing appropriate mechanisms to maximize the use of available funding sources. The foundation implements its programs and interventions in partnership with a network of Palestinian civil society organizations that meet eligibility and due diligence requirements. It has offices in the West Bank, Gaza Strip, Jerusalem, and Lebanon, in addition to offices in Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and Jordan, which can receive funding and support through their bank accounts to finance programs within Palestine. So far, Taawon has successfully supported various development and relief projects and programs with a budget exceeding $950 million, aiming to invest in the Palestinian people, strengthen community resilience, and provide humanitarian support.

Be the change in an orphan’s life.
Sponsor today.

items.content_html:
Gaza is enduring relentless attacks.
Families are displaced, surviving without basic necessities.

Since the first day of the attack, Gaza has faced unthinkable suffering. Thousands of families are forced to survive in inhumane conditions, struggling without food, clean water, and basic healthcare.

It is our responsibility to stand by them now. Your donations would help us provide immediate relief for over 1.7 million displaced individuals. Help us ensure they receive the basic humanitarian needs.

Make a direct impact by contributing to Gaza’s urgent needs today.

The current reality at a glance..

1.7 Million Forcibly Displaced in a Small Area, Representing Only 10% of Gaza

Every day

63 families are displaced

1 out of 3

children in Gaza are malnourished

630,000

students deprived of attending school

Gaza is in crisis. An unprecedented scale of support is needed.

Here’s how we are responding to ensure aid reaches every family in need

Since the onset of the attack, more than half a million individuals have benefited from our interventions. Through the Gaza Emergency Relief Campaign, we are addressing urgent needs such as food, water, healthcare, and shelter for those displaced.

We have partnered with 20 local civil society organizations in Gaza to ensure direct access to displaced families and deliver aid in the toughest circumstances. Alongside our on-ground partners, our global network of supporters is working tirelessly to provide critical support for Gaza.

Areas of intervention

Food & Water

Food parcels &shopping vouchers, fresh produce parcels, and clean water

Healthcare

Medical supplies, and essential services, fuel for hospitals & ambulances

Shelter

Clothes, blankets, and emergency shelter materials

Mental Health Support

Essential Healthcare Services and social welfare

Majdi: A father supporting 8 family members while battling injury

After losing their home and struggling with injuries, your support provided them with essential clothing and hygiene kits, bringing comfort in difficult times.

Soha: A mother’s resilience builds a community kitchen.

Thanks to your support, Soha and her children managed to continue their work, providing 1,500 hot meals to displaced families through Taawon.

A family who lost everything yet refuses to give up.

Thanks to your support, Basem’s family received hygiene kits after losing their home in Gaza.

Shadi’s family finds warmth again

After losing their home and all their belongings, your support provided them with the clothes they need to stay warm.

Taawon

Taawon is an independent collective of Palestinian entrepreneurs, business practitioners, scholars and thinkers, bound together across generations by our dedication for Palestine to persevere and thrive. Since 1983, we have worked to help defend and preserve the Palestinian cause, our culture and our people, by empowering Palestinians and investing in building Palestine's human capital.

Together with local civil society organizations on the ground and a growing network of global support, we have managed to provide life-saving aid to Gaza's most vulnerable. Since the beginning of the attack on Gaza, our relief efforts have focused on providing food, shelter, medical aid, and mental health support to over 520,000 individuals in Gaza.

We are proud of our strong partnerships with more than 20 local organizations who ensure that aid reaches those who need it most, even in the most challenging conditions.

We are available for your inquiries.
Email us at [email protected]

Gaza’s families are counting on us.
Let’s stand by them today.

After losing their home and all their belongings, your support provided them with the clothes they need to stay warm.

Taawon

Taawon is an independent collective of Palestinian entrepreneurs, business practitioners, scholars and thinkers, bound together across generations by our dedication for Palestine to persevere and thrive. Since 1983, we have worked to help defend and preserve the Palestinian cause, our culture and our people, by empowering Palestinians and investing in building Palestine's human capital.

Together with local civil society organizations on the ground and a growing network of global support, we have managed to provide life-saving aid to Gaza's most vulnerable. Since the beginning of the attack on Gaza, our relief efforts have focused on providing food, shelter, medical aid, and mental health support to over 520,000 individuals in Gaza.

We are proud of our strong partnerships with more than 20 local organizations who ensure that aid reaches those who need it most, even in the most challenging conditions.

A crisis in Gaza's education needs an urgent response.

The education system in Gaza has been devastated by ongoing attacks, affecting the dreams and futures of over 88,000 students. Despite these challenges, the ISNAD program aims to provide 30,000 scholarships to support 15,000 students as well as university staff in Gaza, enabling them to resume their studies through distance learning.

The program focuses on major universities such as Al-Azhar University, the Islamic University, and Al-Aqsa University, which collectively serve 72% of Gaza's university students. With a target of raising $16,000,000, ISNAD will cover tuition fees for two semesters, ensuring educational continuity and giving these students the opportunity to build a better future for themselves and for Gaza, thereby enhancing the resilience of Palestinian universities to survive and thrive.

The Short Course on Palestine (September-October 2025), taught by Professor Rashid Khalidi and co-hosted by the People’s Forum and the Institute for Palestine Studies, offers an abbreviated examination of the history of Palestine since 1917…

ISNAD- Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1.    Who does ISNAD support?

ISNAD supports students enrolled in Gaza’s three public universities- Al Azhar, Al Aqsa, and the Islamic University- focusing on those in their final years of study. Priority is given to students in critical specialization that serve the emergency response and future reconstruction, such as health, engineering, education, and agriculture. It also supports students in digitally adaptable fields such as coding and digital marketing, helping them earn remotely and strengthen Gaza’s resilience.

2.    How is ISNAD different from other scholarship programs? 

ISNAD is tailored for crisis conditions. It not only supports students but also sustains Gaza’s public universities, operating through nationally endorsed mechanisms and targeting large-scale, urgent needs. It consolidates scattered emergency initiatives, scaling them into a structured, coordinated, and sustainable platform- aiming to become Palestine’s central scholarship mechanism. 

3.    Where does the donation go? 

All funds are transferred directly to universities through formal financial mechanisms approved by the Palestinian Monetary Authority, ensuring full transparency and accountability. 

4.    Is ISNAD endorsed by national authorities?

Yes. ISNAD operates under the umbrella of the Palestinian Ministry of Education and Higher Education and in partnership with Gaza’s major public universities. 

5.   Can individuals and institutions donate to ISNAD?

Yes. Both individuals and institutions can contribute. Donations can be made via Taawon’s website here, or by contacting our fundraising team for partnership opportunities at ([email protected] ).

6.    How is impact measured and reported? 

Through its steering committee and university representatives, Taawon monitors enrollment and graduation data, collects student surveys and testimonials, and receives university feedback and reports. 

7.    Why support students in Gaza’s universities instead of the emergency initiatives by universities themselves? 

ISNAD complements and coordinates partners' efforts under one structured, applicable national mechanism. ISNAD reduces duplication, ensures equal access, and aligns with Gaza’s reconstruction and educational recovery priorities. 

Scattered efforts can weaken impact; ISNAD scales them strategically. 
 

8.    What about internet access and digital barriers? 

ISNAD recognizes connectivity as a major barrier. ISNAD works closely with universities and local partners to provide flexible learning options and support, including printed materials, offline access tools, and targeted digital access solutions whenever possible, building on the lessons of COVID and the realities of the aggression. 

We are also seeking partnerships to establish internet access hubs and digital learning solutions across Gaza. 

9.    How does ISNAD operate amid Gaza’s famine and humanitarian crisis? 

ISNAD treats education as a lifeline, operating as an educational survival strategy- ensuring students remain connected to learning, purpose, and hope. Even amid famine, students attend remote classes and complete exams. ISNAD gives them a path forward when everything else is collapsing. 

10.    What is the long-term vision for ISNAD after the aggression? 

ISNAD seeks to prevent the collapse of Gaza’s higher education, and contributes to the steadfastness and resilience of national institutions by keeping students enrolled, supporting faculty, and preserving institutional continuity during aggression- laying the foundation for long-term recovery and development through (providing scholarship to majors that have direct impact to the current context and contributes to the reconstruction phase. 

11.    Why focus on the three public universities?

These universities make up 78% of Gaza’s student population, and are public institutions, public universities, relying on governmental finances to continue operating, which cannot happen in the current political landscape. 

About Taawon

Taawon is an independent collective of Palestinian entrepreneurs, business practitioners, scholars and thinkers, bound together across generations by our dedication for Palestine to persevere and thrive.
Since our establishment in 1983, Taawon has consistently worked to defend and preserve Palestinian culture and heritage, empowering communities and investing in human capital. Our interventions have included extensive support for the education sector, with $276,000,000 allocated to educational programs from 1983 to 2023. We work closely with local civil society organizations and a global support network to address the diverse needs of Palestinians.

We are available for your inquiries.

Al-Bireh, Palestine — 1 September 2026 — Taawon (Welfare Association), Inash Al-Usra Association, and the Palestinian Museum have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to collaborate on a new art project entitled “When the Canvas Weaves into the Thobe.” The partnership brings together three institutions that have each sustained ongoing efforts to preserve Palestinian cultural life, now join forces on a shared project where embroidery meets painting.

The collection features six embroidered thobes inspired by the paintings of renowned artist Suleiman Mansour, creating a dynamic dialogue between two distinct Palestinian artistic traditions: fine art and traditional embroidery. Selected details from Mansour’s decades-long portfolio depicting the Palestinian landscape and its people are translated into thread and fabric — a medium long used by Palestinian women across generations to record place, belonging, and identity.

Rather than simply reproducing the paintings, the craft reinterprets Mansour's work. Through this exchange, embroidery becomes a medium through which his art finds new expression, creating a bridge between past and present and affirming the continuity of Palestinian culture within contemporary practice.

Under the agreement, the three institutions will work together to develop, exhibit, and promote the collection through partnerships with international museums and cultural institutions, host exhibitions, and organize tours both within Palestine and abroad.

For Taawon, this partnership extends a commitment that runs through all of its work: that Palestinian identity, heritage, and cultural memory are not simply to be archived, but are living practices carried forward by each generation. The collaboration sits within Taawon’s wider mission — investing in people, sustaining communities, and responding to humanitarian need — where cultural continuity is a vital part of community resilience.

Every child deserves the opportunity to grow up surrounded by care, protected with dignity, and given the chance to look toward the future with hope. Yet since October 2023, the war in Gaza has left more than 58,000 children without one or both parents, creating an unprecedented need for sustained care and protection.

The Justice Company Humanitarian Foundation https://www.justicecompanyfoundation.com/, supported by The Justice Company www.justicecompany.com, supports carefully selected humanitarian initiatives that expand opportunity, strengthen resilience, and improve outcomes for vulnerable individuals and communities. Through this commitment, the Foundation has partnered with Taawon to support 250 orphaned children in Gaza through the NOOR Orphan Care Program.

Developed by Taawon in response to the war in Gaza, the NOOR Orphan Care Program is built on the belief that no child should have to face such profound loss alone. More than a sponsorship programme, NOOR is a comprehensive, long-term initiative that combines immediate humanitarian support with long-term human development. Through healthcare, education, humanitarian assistance, mental health and psychosocial support, and social care, the programme walks alongside children throughout their journey, helping them heal, regain stability, remain protected, and build a future filled with dignity and hope.

The Foundation's support reflects a shared belief that children who have experienced profound loss deserve more than short-term assistance. They deserve the opportunity to continue learning, recover in a safe and supportive environment, and grow into healthy, resilient young people despite the extraordinary challenges they have faced.

For the 250 children supported through this partnership, NOOR represents far more than humanitarian assistance. It offers continuity of care, stability, and the reassurance that they are not alone, that someone is walking beside them, investing in their wellbeing, and helping them shape a brighter future.

Together, the Foundation and Taawon are investing in more than meeting today's needs. They are helping restore hope, strengthen resilience, and ensure that orphaned children have the opportunity to heal, thrive, and build the future they deserve.

NOOR is Taawon's flagship national initiative for the care of Gaza's orphaned children, providing an integrated model of support that accompanies children from emergency response through long-term recovery and development.
